'''''Cassinia''''' is a genus of about fifty-two species of flowering plants in the family [[Asteraceae]] that are native to Australia and New Zealand. Plants in the genus ''Cassinia'' are shrubs, sometimes small trees with leaves arranged alternately, and [[Head (botany)|heads]] of white, cream-coloured, yellow or pinkish flowers surrounded by several rows of [[bract]]s.

==Description==
Plants in the genus ''Cassinia'' are shrubs or small trees, sometimes with sticky foliage. The leaves are arranged alternately, the edges flat to strongly rolled under, and the flowers white to cream-coloured, yellow or pinkish, arranged in heads, the heads in cylindrical, top-shaped or bell-shaped [[corymb]]s. The heads are surrounded by several rows of usually erect, boat-shaped bracts. The [[Glossary of botanical terms#floret|florets]] are [[Plant reproductive morphology#Bisexual|bisexual]] and cylindrical with five lobes and the [[Cypsela (botany)|cypselas]] are small and usually have a [[Pappus (botany)|pappus]] of bristles.<ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |title=''Cassinia'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/a6465585-5699-4b95-bab7-d8ead66a05d0 |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref><ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |title=Genus ''Cassinia'' |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&showsyn=&dist=&constat=&lvl=gn&name=Cassinia |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref><ref name="efloraSA">{{cite web |title=''Cassinia'' |url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/cgi-bin/speciesfacts_display.cgi?form=speciesfacts&name=Cassinia |publisher=State Herbarium of South Australia |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The genus ''Cassinia'' was first formally described in 1817 by [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]] in his book ''Observations on the Natural Family of Plants called Compositae''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Cassinia''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/734597|publisher=APNI|accessdate=4 June 2021}}</ref><ref name="R.Br.">{{cite book |last1=Brown |first1=Robert |title=Observations on the Natural Family of Plants called Compositae |date=1817 |location=London |page=126 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/237821#page/58/mode/1up |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref> Brown had previously used the name ''Cassinia'' in the second edition of the ''[[Hortus Kewensis]]'' but the name was not validly published because no species was described.<ref name=APNI1>{{cite web|title=''Cassinia'' nom. rej.|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/734598|publisher=APNI|accessdate=4 June 2021}}</ref><ref name="Hortus">{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=Robert |title=''Cassinia'' |journal=Hortus Kewensis |date=1813 |edition=2 |volume=5 |pages=184–185 |url=https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/12184/?offset=#page=186&viewer=picture&o=bookmark&n=0&q= |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref>

The genus was named for French botanist [[Alexandre de Cassini]].<ref name="Sharr">{{cite book |last1=Sharr |first1=Francis Aubi |last2=George |first2=Alex |title=Western Australian Plant Names and Their Meanings |date=2019 |publisher=Four Gables Press |location=Kardinya, WA |isbn=9780958034180 |page=67 |edition=3rd}}</ref>
